title: “If he feels a pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent.’ He understands: ‘I am not attached to it.’ He understands: ‘I do not delight…
content: “If he feels a pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent.’ He understands: ‘I am not attached to it.’ He understands: ‘I do not delight in it.’ If he feels a painful feeling … If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent.’ He understands: ‘I am not attached to it.’ He understands: ‘I do not delight in it.’ If he feels a pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is not bound. If he feels a painful feeling, he feels it as one who is not bound. If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is not bound. When he feels a feeling ending with the body, he understands: ‘I feel a feeling ending with the body.’ When he feels a feeling ending with life, he understands: ‘I feel a feeling ending with life.’ He understands: ‘With the breakup of the body, after death, everything that is felt, in which he no longer delights, will become cool right here.’”

title: “Householders, if those wanderers of other sects ask you: ‘By what basis, by what tradition, do you speak of those venerable ones as follows: Surely…
content: “Householders, if those wanderers of other sects ask you: ‘By what basis, by what tradition, do you speak of those venerable ones as follows: Surely those venerable ones are free from lust, or are on the path to subduing lust; free from ill-will, or on the path to subduing ill-will; free from delusion, or on the path to subduing delusion?’—when asked thus, householders, you should answer those wanderers of other sects: ‘Those venerable ones dwell in remote lodgings in isolated forests. But in such places there are no forms cognizable by the eye that they could see and then delight in; no sounds cognizable by the ear … no odors cognizable by the nose … no tastes cognizable by the tongue … no tangibles cognizable by the body that they could feel and then delight in. Good sirs, by this basis, by this tradition, we speak of those venerable ones as follows: Surely those venerable ones are free from lust, or are on the path to subduing lust; free from ill-will … free from delusion, or on the path to subduing delusion.’”

title: “Here, monks, a person truly understands the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to sensual pleasures. By truly understanding…
content: “Here, monks, a person truly understands the origination, the cessation, the gratification, the peril, and the escape in regard to sensual pleasures. By truly understanding them, sensual desire, sensual delight, sensual attachment, sensual infatuation, sensual thirst, sensual fever, sensual clinging, sensual craving regarding sensual pleasures do not invade and remain. This, monks, is called freedom from the yoke of sensual desire.”

title: “This city is built of bones, Plastered with flesh and blood; Within dwells aging and death, Conceit and hypocrisy.” “Even the king’s splendid chariot wears…
content:
“This city is built of bones,
Plastered with flesh and blood;
Within dwells aging and death,
Conceit and hypocrisy.”

“Even the king’s splendid chariot wears out,
So too this body eventually ages.
But the Dhamma of the good does not age —
So the good indeed speak to the good.”

“A person of little learning,
Like an ox, grows old;
His flesh increases,
But not his wisdom.”

title: “Sunakkhatta, suppose there is a very poisonous viper. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering.…
content:
“Sunakkhatta, suppose there is a very poisonous viper. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Would that man give his hand or his foot to that viper if he knew: ‘If I am bitten by this snake, I will meet death or deadly suffering’?”
“No, venerable sir.”
“So too, Sunakkhatta, a monk should surely guard himself in regard to the six sense-bases. Knowing that ‘Attachment is the root of suffering,’ he becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. It does not happen that he would still focus his body on attachment or direct his mind to attachment.”

title: “Monks, wander in your own proper range, in your own ancestral territory. Monks, if you wander in your own proper range, in your own ancestral…
content: “Monks, wander in your own proper range, in your own ancestral territory. Monks, if you wander in your own proper range, in your own ancestral territory, then longevity will increase, beauty will increase, ease will increase, wealth will increase, power will increase.”

title: “So too, venerable sirs, the eye is not the bondage of forms, nor are forms the bondage of the eye. Whatever desire and lust arises…
content: “So too, venerable sirs, the eye is not the bondage of forms, nor are forms the bondage of the eye. Whatever desire and lust arises in dependence on both — that is the bondage there. The ear is not the bondage of sounds … The nose is not the bondage of odors … The tongue is not the bondage of tastes … The body is not the bondage of touches … The mind is not the bondage of phenomena, nor are phenomena the bondage of the mind. Whatever desire and lust arises in dependence on both — that is the bondage there.”

title: “Monks, whatever is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being. And what, monks, is not yours? Form, monks, is…
content: “Monks, whatever is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being. And what, monks, is not yours? Form, monks, is not yours — abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being. Feeling … Perception … Formations … Consciousness is not yours — abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your happiness and well-being.”

title: “Monks, what is clinging and worry? Here, monks, an untaught ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained…
content: “Monks, what is clinging and worry? Here, monks, an untaught ordinary person, not seeing the noble ones, not skilled in the noble Dhamma, not trained in the noble Dhamma, not seeing the true persons, not skilled in the true Dhamma, not trained in the true Dhamma, regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form. For him, that form changes and alters. Because of the change and alteration of form, his consciousness follows that change in form. Worrying states arise from that consciousness following the change in form, invading his mind and remaining. Because his mind is invaded, he is terrified, distressed, and full of longing and worry.”

title: Elder Mahā-Moggallāna: With hut whose roof is made of bones, Sewn together with sinews and flesh — Foul, full of stench! Carrying other people’s limbs…
content:
Elder Mahā-Moggallāna:

With hut whose roof is made of bones,
Sewn together with sinews and flesh —
Foul, full of stench!
Carrying other people’s limbs
As my own body!

The container full of feces,
Covered over with skin —
O female demon!
With your breasts like boils —
Your body has nine streams,
Always flowing.

Your body’s nine streams,
Foul, creating bondage —
The monk avoids that body
As a clean person avoids feces.

If others knew you
As I know you,
They would avoid you
As one avoids feces in the rain.

It is truly so, O Great Hero,
As the ascetic said:
Here, some are stuck,
Like an old ox in the mud.

One who thinks he can dye
The sky with turmeric,
Or with any other color —
That one only fails.

My mind is like that sky —
Well concentrated internally —
Do not bring evil thoughts to it,
Like a bird falling into a pile of fire.
